sentences.text: Complete fossil specimens representing both male and female individuals of S. polyspondyla are known.
A second species, S. tenuispina, known only from an isolated male horn, is now considered the same species as S. polyspondyla.
The type specimen of Squaloraja was discovered by Mary Anning in 1829.
The type specimen was held at the Bristol Museum but was destroyed during The Blitz, except for the tail.
Louis Agassiz described the species as Spinacorhinus polyspondylus in 1836 based on the same specimen.
Agassiz changed the genus name to Squaloraja in 1843 but kept his original species name.
Research suggests Squaloraja was a relict taxon and the last survivor of a chimaera lineage that diverged from Chimaeroidei by the late Mississippian stage of the Carboniferous period.
Squaloraja belongs to the parent group Squalorajidae.
Squaloraja is classified in the family Squalorajidae.
Squaloraja is classified in the class Chondrichthyes.
The named species S. polyspondyla was found in the Sinemurian-aged Blue Lias formation of Lyme Regis, England.
A complete female specimen of an indeterminate Squaloraja species was found in the Sinemurian-aged Moltrasio Formation of Osteno, Italy.
Indeterminate teeth of Squaloraja have been found in the earlier Hettangian period of Belgium.
Squaloraja lived from the Hettangian to the Sinemurian, between 201.4 and 192.9 million years ago.
